description: Governance Contract (OAGE P1.0). Declares, for every policy file, WHO has the authority to apply it and HOW that authority is proven. A policy is not enforcement until the chain Policy -> Consumer -> Enforcement -> Adversarial Test -> CI exists; this file is where the chain is declared, and scripts/governance-doctor.mjs is what confronts the declaration with reality.

authorities.kernel: Runtime enforcement inside .opencode/plugins. Blocks the tool call itself, before it happens.
authorities.phase: Enforced at a phase boundary (completion/review), by scripts that take --phase.
authorities.handoff: Enforced when work passes between agents, where agent identity actually exists.
authorities.ci: Enforced by CI, independently of anything the agent claims.
authorities.declarative: Not enforced. Configuration or documentation consumed by tooling.

enforcementModes.runtime: Read by a plugin on tool.execute.before / .after.
enforcementModes.phase: Read by evidence-check / reviewer-check / state-manager at a phase transition.
enforcementModes.declarative: Read only by generators, installers or validators.

failureModes.escalate: Violation warns and escalates to human review rather than blocking outright.

statuses.enforced: A real consumer applies this policy. The doctor verifies the consumer exists and references it.
statuses.unenforced: Declared intent with no consumer yet. A tracked gap: the doctor reports UNENFORCED_POLICY.

protected-resources.json.note: KERNEL_SELF_PROTECTION. The one policy that guards the kernel against itself.

behavior-contract.json.note: Supplies riskEscalation, which is why a critical phase raises HIGH to CRITICAL.

policy-resolver.json.note: The real source of the context7/truth/skill/knowledge action policies — not context7-gate.json or skill-gate.json.

loop-detector.json.note: P1.1: scores behavioural risk instead of counting calls, and the WARN -> ESCALATE -> BLOCK ladder now matches this failureMode. Previously it blocked outright on the 4th identical attempt, was reachable only from bash (write/edit returned from the before hook first), and keyed on the raw target so re-spelling a path evaded it.

tool-gate.json.note: oage-enforce.js applies rules[] (deny/block/ask/allow) and globalRules.forbiddenPatterns directly in tool.execute.before, for every rule except 'git-commit' — the kernel cannot run lint/typecheck/test/coverage itself, so that one rule stays audit-only (event quality_gate_check). Until this was wired in, only tool-guard.ps1 (a script nothing calls automatically) enforced deny/ask, so 'destructive'/'git-push'/'prisma-schema' and forbiddenPatterns were declared enforced but live-inert.

state-machine.json.note: Read fresh on every call, not cached — /agent_loop rewrites currentState mid-session.

audit.json.note: P1.2 Phase 2: Retention enforcement via rotation engine. maxAge/maxSize now implemented. current.jsonl bounded at 10MB/10K events. Archive preserves historical events for forensic purposes.

definition-of-done.json.note: Not in CI yet: evidence-check needs --phase, so it cannot run on every push. P1.4 derives the phase from state-machine.json.

reviewer-gate.json.note: Separation of duties. Cannot be a kernel policy: tool.execute.before carries no agent identity, so 'a different agent than the implementer' is only decidable where attribution is explicit.

permissions-matrix.json.note: Phase-scoped allowedAgents. Deliberately NOT a kernel policy — the runtime hook has no agent identity, so pushing it into tool.execute.before would create a false sense of enforcement. Its only consumer today is a PowerShell guard, which does not run on non-Windows or in CI: P1.3 gives it real authority at handoff/CI.

skill-gate.json.note: The RUNTIME skill gate does not read this file — it resolves from policy-resolver.json plus skill-engine's technology map. This file governs the phase-level pipeline only.

ci-gate.json.note: scripts/ci-gate-check.mjs reads ci-gate.json and fails the pipeline when a required check has no step in the workflow, unless skipIfMissing legitimately skips it.

security-gates.json.note: scripts/lint.mjs reads security-gates.json as the source of the security scan rules and CI runs it via the anti-patterns step. Deploy-time security signoff remains a tracked gap.

production-gate.json.note: Deploy-time gate, not a per-push gate: requireHumanApproval and approvalRequired.roles=human need a human, and the thresholds (coverage >= 80, performance >= 90) need evidence that does not exist at push time. Kept as a tracked gap until a release/deploy pipeline consumes it.

context7-gate.json.note: The runtime context7 requirement comes from policy-resolver.json's actions.context7, NOT from this file. It looks like the source of that gate and is not.

skill-gate-auto.json.note: Automatic skill resolution is hardcoded in .opencode/plugins/lib/skill-engine.js instead of being driven by this file.

mcp-registry.json.note: A registry of permitted MCP servers. Shape is validated; nothing gates MCP usage on it.

memory.json.note: Shape only: generated into projects and validated. The memory FILES under .opencode/memory/ are what the scripts actually read.

blueprint.json.note: Only present in projects installed via --blueprint.

opencode.json.note: The OpenCode project config, not a governance policy. Lives at the project root in installed projects.

governance-state.json.note: SOURCE OF DECISION for Context7/Skill/Version gates. Validated schema (version, schemaVersion, projectId, createdAt, updatedAt, entries[]). Entries have TTL (context7: 30m, skill: 60m, version: 120m). Dual-write: audit hook writes state, enforce hook reads state. INDEPENDENT from audit.jsonl (SOURCE OF EXPLANATION). Cross-session isolation: session A evidence does not satisfy session B.
